# pip install obspy pandas
import pandas as pd
from obspy import UTCDateTime
from obspy.clients.fdsn import Client

client = Client('https://service.earthscope.org')
NET, STA, LOC = 'OO', 'AXBA1', '10'
t1, t2 = UTCDateTime("2025-03-01T00:00:00"), UTCDateTime("2025-03-02T00:00:00")   # the timeframe, UTC
TEMPERATURE = {"UDO": "UK1", "LDO": "LK1"}   # each pressure channel's housing temperature

# Which pressure channel recorded which part of the timeframe (UDO every 15 s, LDO at 1 Hz).
inv = client.get_stations(network=NET, station=STA, location=LOC, channel="UDO,LDO", starttime=t1, endtime=t2, level="channel")
parts = []
for cha in inv[0][0]:
    a, b = max(t1, cha.start_date), min(t2, cha.end_date) if cha.end_date else t2
    if a >= b:
        continue
    st = client.get_waveforms(NET, STA, LOC, f"{cha.code},{TEMPERATURE[cha.code]}", a, b)
    st.merge(method=1, fill_value=None)
    # Already pascals and degrees C: no remove_sensitivity or remove_response (see above).
    columns = {}
    for tr in st:
        name = "pressure_pa" if tr.stats.channel == cha.code else "housing_temperature_c"
        t = pd.to_datetime(tr.times("timestamp"), unit="s", utc=True).round("s")
        columns[name] = pd.Series(tr.data.astype(float), index=t)
    df = pd.DataFrame(columns)
    df["channel"] = cha.code
    parts.append(df)
    print(f"{cha.code} ({cha.sample_rate:g} Hz): {a} to {b}, {len(df)} samples")

data = pd.concat(parts).sort_index()
data.index.name = "time_utc"
out = f"{NET}.{STA}.{LOC}_pressure_{t1.date}_{t2.date}.csv"
data.to_csv(out)
print(f"wrote {out}: {len(data)} rows, {data.pressure_pa.min():.0f} to {data.pressure_pa.max():.0f} Pa")

from obspy.clients.fdsn import Client

client = Client('https://service.earthscope.org')
NET, STA, LOC = 'OO', 'AXBA1', '20'
t1, t2 = UTCDateTime("2025-03-01T00:00:00"), UTCDateTime("2025-03-01T06:00:00")   # the timeframe, UTC

    columns[NAMES[tr.stats.channel]] = pd.Series(np.ma.filled(np.ma.array(tr.data, dtype=float), np.nan), index=t)

results.question: Give me Python code to download Axial Seamount Central Caldera Tiltmeter/Accelerometer Station AXCC2 (EARTHSCOPE-OO-AXCC2) data from 2021-08-25 23:59 to 2021-08-26 00:09 UTC
results.code:
# pip install obspy
import numpy as np
from obspy import UTCDateTime
from obspy.clients.fdsn import Client

client = Client('https://service.earthscope.org')
t1, t2 = UTCDateTime("2021-08-25T23:59:00"), UTCDateTime("2021-08-26T00:09:00")   # the timeframe, UTC
st = client.get_waveforms('OO', 'AXCC2', "*", 'BNZ', t1, t2)
inv = client.get_stations(network='OO', station='AXCC2', channel='BNZ', starttime=t1, endtime=t2, level="response")
# Counts to ground acceleration in m/s**2; leave this loop out for raw counts. The pre-filter tapers the spectrum off outside
# the band the instrument records (the flat part of its response, below Nyquist), where dividing by its tiny
# response would blow up noise.
for tr in st:
    f = np.logspace(-4, np.log10(tr.stats.sampling_rate / 2), 500)
    amp = np.abs(inv.get_response(tr.id, tr.stats.starttime).get_evalresp_response_for_frequencies(f, output="DEF"))
    flat = f[amp >= amp.max() / np.sqrt(2)]
    low = max(flat[0], 2 / (tr.stats.endtime - tr.stats.starttime))   # no lower than the record resolves
    high = min(flat[-1], 0.45 * tr.stats.sampling_rate)
    tr.detrend("linear")
    tr.remove_response(inventory=inv, output='ACC', pre_filt=(low / 2, low, 0.8 * high, high), water_level=None)
st.write('OO.AXCC2.BNZ_' + f"{t1.date}.mseed", format="MSEED")

# pip install requests xarray netCDF4
import re, requests, xarray as xr

DATASET = 'RS01SLBS-LJ01A-11-OPTAAC103-streamed-optaa_sample'
VARIABLES = ['elapsed_run_time']   # any of the stream's variables listed above
START, END = "2026-10-26T11:03:00", "2026-10-26T12:03:00"   # the timeframe, UTC
T = 'https://thredds.dataexplorer.oceanobservatories.org/thredds'
stamp = lambda t: t.replace("-", "").replace(":", "")[:15]
xml = requests.get(f"{T}/catalog/ooigoldcopy/public/{DATASET}/catalog.xml", timeout=120).text
paths = [p for p in re.findall(r'urlPath="([^"]+\.nc)"', xml)
         if (s := re.search(r'_(\d{8}T\d{6})[.\d]*-(\d{8}T\d{6})[.\d]*\.nc$', p))
         and s.group(2) >= stamp(START) and s.group(1) <= stamp(END)]
parts = []
for path in paths:
    ds = xr.open_dataset(f"{T}/dodsC/{path}")   # OPeNDAP: nothing is read until .load()
    ds = (ds.swap_dims({"obs": "time"}) if "obs" in ds.dims else ds).reset_coords()   # depth becomes a variable
    wanted = [v for v in VARIABLES if v in ds.variables]   # a file can lack one (the newest, not yet processed)
    if wanted:
        parts.append(ds[wanted].sel(time=slice(START, END)).load())
if not parts:
    raise SystemExit(f"no {VARIABLES} in {DATASET} between {START} and {END}")
data = xr.concat(parts, dim="time", data_vars="all", join="outer")   # what a file lacks is NaN
data.encoding.pop("unlimited_dims", None)
data.to_netcdf(f"{DATASET}_{stamp(START)}_{stamp(END)}.nc")   # or data.to_dataframe().to_csv(...)

results.code:
# pip install obspy pandas
import pandas as pd
from obspy import UTCDateTime
from obspy.clients.fdsn import Client

client = Client('https://service.earthscope.org')
NET, STA, LOC = 'OO', 'HYSB1', '10'
t1, t2 = UTCDateTime("2025-03-01T00:00:00"), UTCDateTime("2025-03-02T00:00:00")   # the timeframe, UTC
TEMPERATURE = {"UDO": "UK1", "LDO": "LK1"}   # each pressure channel's housing temperature

# Which pressure channel recorded which part of the timeframe (UDO every 15 s, LDO at 1 Hz).
inv = client.get_stations(network=NET, station=STA, location=LOC, channel="UDO,LDO", starttime=t1, endtime=t2, level="channel")
parts = []
for cha in inv[0][0]:
    a, b = max(t1, cha.start_date), min(t2, cha.end_date) if cha.end_date else t2
    if a >= b:
        continue
    st = client.get_waveforms(NET, STA, LOC, f"{cha.code},{TEMPERATURE[cha.code]}", a, b)
    st.merge(method=1, fill_value=None)
    # Already pascals and degrees C: no remove_sensitivity or remove_response (see above).
    columns = {}
    for tr in st:
        name = "pressure_pa" if tr.stats.channel == cha.code else "housing_temperature_c"
        t = pd.to_datetime(tr.times("timestamp"), unit="s", utc=True).round("s")
        columns[name] = pd.Series(tr.data.astype(float), index=t)
    df = pd.DataFrame(columns)
    df["channel"] = cha.code
    parts.append(df)
    print(f"{cha.code} ({cha.sample_rate:g} Hz): {a} to {b}, {len(df)} samples")

data = pd.concat(parts).sort_index()
data.index.name = "time_utc"
out = f"{NET}.{STA}.{LOC}_pressure_{t1.date}_{t2.date}.csv"
data.to_csv(out)
print(f"wrote {out}: {len(data)} rows, {data.pressure_pa.min():.0f} to {data.pressure_pa.max():.0f} Pa")

results.question: Give me Python code to download Southern Hydrate Ridge Summit Seismic Station HYS13 (EARTHSCOPE-OO-HYS13) data from 2026-10-26 08:21 to 2026-10-26 08:31 UTC
results.code:
# pip install obspy
import numpy as np
from obspy import UTCDateTime
from obspy.clients.fdsn import Client

client = Client('https://service.earthscope.org')
t1, t2 = UTCDateTime("2026-10-26T08:21:00"), UTCDateTime("2026-10-26T08:31:00")   # the timeframe, UTC
st = client.get_waveforms('OO', 'HYS13', "*", 'EHZ', t1, t2)
inv = client.get_stations(network='OO', station='HYS13', channel='EHZ', starttime=t1, endtime=t2, level="response")
# Counts to ground velocity in m/s; leave this loop out for raw counts. The pre-filter tapers the spectrum off outside
# the band the instrument records (the flat part of its response, below Nyquist), where dividing by its tiny
# response would blow up noise.
for tr in st:
    f = np.logspace(-4, np.log10(tr.stats.sampling_rate / 2), 500)
    amp = np.abs(inv.get_response(tr.id, tr.stats.starttime).get_evalresp_response_for_frequencies(f, output="DEF"))
    flat = f[amp >= amp.max() / np.sqrt(2)]
    low = max(flat[0], 2 / (tr.stats.endtime - tr.stats.starttime))   # no lower than the record resolves
    high = min(flat[-1], 0.45 * tr.stats.sampling_rate)
    tr.detrend("linear")
    tr.remove_response(inventory=inv, output='VEL', pre_filt=(low / 2, low, 0.8 * high, high), water_level=None)
st.write('OO.HYS13.EHZ_' + f"{t1.date}.mseed", format="MSEED")
